News summary:

Cisco introduces Ecosystem Deal Registration alongside new incentives and AI-enabled tools for partners to recognize and support our ecosystem at every step of the deal.

General availability of Cisco IQ for partners provides new profitability avenues and growth opportunities.

Expanded Cisco Cloud Control offerings provide partners with new ways to build, secure, and manage AI-ready infrastructure.

VANCOUVER, BC – October 26, 2026 – AI is moving infrastructure to the center of enterprise investment, creating a critical market opportunity to modernize, scale, and secure the networks that power the AI era. To help its partners lead this transformation, today at Cisco Partner Summit, Cisco (NASDAQ: CSCO) unveiled new advancements across its partner program, customer experience offerings and technology portfolio, providing the tools and incentives required to capture this next wave of global connectivity growth.

Expanded incentives within the Cisco 360 Partner Program combined with the general availability of Cisco IQ for Partners address the demand for more agility and intelligence in the current environment. Cisco Cloud Control continues to bring it all together, giving Cisco partners, IT professionals and AI agents a platform where they can work together to connect, protect and run the critical infrastructure for the AI era.

“Our partners are where Cisco meets the customer, and the AI era is asking more of all of us,” said Tim Coogan, SVP, Global Partner Sales, Cisco. "Customers need partners with the agility to move first and fast. By combining the strength of the Cisco 360 Partner Program with Cisco IQ and Cisco Cloud Control, we’re giving every type of partner new ways to deliver that and be rewarded for it, from the advisor who shapes a decision to the partner who delivers and supports it."

Powering an Agile Partner Ecosystem

Advisors, Developers, and Distributors increasingly shape what customers buy as well as how it's delivered, and as the Cisco 360 Partner Program enters its first full year, the program has added dedicated paths for each of them. Additional enhancements span program experience, profitability and enablement for all partner types, empowering true ecosystem agility in the AI era, and rewarding the contributions of every partner.

Ecosystem Deal Registration: A new way for Advisors and Developers to be formally recognized for contributions that lead to transactions, validating partner impact across the customer lifecycle.

New growth paths: Advisor and Developer Partner Value Indexes (PVIs) are now available and a new unified Distributor PVI will be available by Spring of 2027, underscoring Cisco’s commitment to measuring partner contributions based on the unique value their role brings to the customer.

Evolution of Cisco Partner Incentive (CPI) Rates: A continued investment in partner value exchange,increasing ACV growth reward by 50% as well as a 2x increase on Adopt for all use cases, as well as launching new adopt incentives on Cisco IQ.

Additional +2% Cross-Sell Bonus: An incremental +2% on top of the existing cross-sell rebate for Preferred and Portfolio partners expanding customer accounts into net-new Cisco architectures, including Splunk.

Cisco IQ Adopt Incentive: Designed to reward Partner adoption of Cisco IQ to ensure customers are onboarded and integrated with their telemetry.

Additionally, enhanced partner experience resources are now available to help partners differentiate and expand their offerings for customers:

Deal registration visibility in Partner Experience Platform (PXP): Automated, real-time insights to optimize pipeline health and enable partners to identify growth opportunities.

Advanced Trend Analysis and Eligibility Tracking: New PVI APIs enable partners to optimize their business outcomes and proactively manage their performance.

On-demand agentic resource: The One Cisco Content Agent (beta) makes it easy for partner sellers and marketers to quickly access approved Cisco content and customize value propositions for every customer tailored to specific priorities and industry trends, creating relevant co-branded presentations in minutes rather than hours.

New CPI Deal Estimator: Empowers partners to model deal economics and optimize rebate yield across every opportunity.

New OT certification: To reflect the growing convergence of IT, OT, and security, Learn with Cisco is launching a new Cisco OT Security Practitioner certification and releasing Cisco Modeling Labs 2.11 with new hands-on lab capabilities.

Cisco IQ: New Partner Opportunities for Profitable Services

Customers crave the ability to better understand their IT environments, intuitively identify risk, and quickly act before issues impact business outcomes. Partners need that same level of visibility so they can deliver more relevant, higher-value services to customers and propose modernization opportunities. Today, Cisco is announcing the general availability of Cisco IQ for Partners, empowering its global partner ecosystem to drive repeatable, high-margin growth across both managed services and reseller models. With more than 16,000 customers, and with visibility across close to 20 million devices since April 2026, the extension of Cisco IQ to partners provides new opportunities for growth after deal closure:

Deliver differentiated managed services: With Cisco IQ MCP Server and expanded API access, partners can seamlessly integrate intelligence into their own professional services, workflows, and AI agents. This enables partners to instantly query customer estates so they can address short term risks like emerging AI-powered threats, while helping customers plan for infrastructure modernization.

Secure, automated capabilities for Resellers: Through new Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) in Cisco IQ, customers can grant partners direct, secure visibility into their installed base. This transforms resellers into intelligence-led partners who can leverage real-time data and APIs to operate at machine scale—spotting hidden network risks, eliminating manual exports, and proactively driving customer modernization.

Cisco is also introducing new Cisco IQ capabilities for customers and partners:

New AI-Powered Quantum Safe and Software End of Vulnerability Support (EoVS)playbooks to help identify risks beyond routine patching.

Priority Bugs & Software Conformance Assessments to spot outage risks, prioritize remediation, and scope upgrades or hardening services.

Frictionless Cisco Cloud Control integration surfacing real-time risk intelligence, including quantum-readiness status, and enabling one-click action on at-risk, controller-managed devices directly within Cloud Control.

Cisco IQ AI Assistant enhancements based on rich contextual real-time data with troubleshooting now informed by device diagnostics and Cisco Technical Assistance Center (TAC) knowledge. Simplified TAC case management means you can create, close, and escalate a TAC case from within the AI Assistant.

"For too long, partners walked into customer conversations without the same view Cisco had. That changes today,” said Liz Centoni, EVP and Chief Customer Experience Officer, Cisco.

“With Cisco IQ Partner Support Standard, partners get that same intelligence under their own brand, delivered through their own experts. It's their name. Their customer relationship. Their services practice. Cisco IQ is the engine. Partners are the business."

Resilient, Secure, and AI-Ready Infrastructure Innovations

As enterprises scale AI agents across wired and wireless networks, they face mounting risks from downtime, visibility gaps, and identity-based threats. Cisco Cloud Control addresses these challenges by providing a shared, unified operations platform for teams and AI agents to secure and manage critical infrastructure across IT domains. To further enable machine-speed collaboration and automation, we are introducing new AgenticOps capabilities to Cloud Control, including:

Model Foundry:A new platform service in Cisco Cloud Control for putting Cisco’s purpose-built models to work — discovering, evaluating, fine-tuning, and running them on your own data, all in one place. Model Foundry is also the exclusive home of Cisco’s newest model versions and weights before broader release. Controlled Availability begins with Cisco partners.

ThousandEyes intelligence for trusted autonomous operations: Cisco is integrating ThousandEyes natively into Wi-Fi 6E and 7 access points, included with eligible Cisco Networking Essentials and Advantage licenses. With nothing additional to buy, deploy, or configure, always-on ThousandEyes enables automated background testing that is designed to validate application and network performance around the clock even when no users are online and strengthens customer trust in agentic actions.

Agentic integration: Cisco is introducing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for its networking platforms, which act as a standardized bridge that allows AI tools to easily access live network data. This removes the need for partners to build and maintain complex custom connections, making it simpler to create automated workflows for tasks like troubleshooting and reporting, while helping IT teams identify and resolve issues faster by linking deep telemetry directly to actionable experience metrics.

“The future of infrastructure operations is agentic, and it requires a platform that combines shared context, purpose-built models, and clear guardrails. Cisco Cloud Control is that platform,” said Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer, Cisco. “With the new Model Foundry, we’re advancing the state of the art in AgenticOps further. Enabling partners to fine-tune and customize Cisco’s models for their customers’ environments will make them integral to how their customers connect, protect, and run their infrastructure.”

To deliver the hardened physical and digital foundation required to connect, power, and protect mission-critical workloads for the long term, Cisco is introducing new resilient and quantum-safe innovations, including:

Extending quantum readiness across wireless networks: Cisco is launching the industry's first Wi-Fi 7 access point with quantum-resilient capabilities. This is the latest addition to the most comprehensive quantum-resilient networking portfolio, spanning wireless, switching, and routing, enabling partners to deliver quantum-readiness assessments and future-proof customer infrastructure investments well into the next decade. For quantum-safe communications with Post Quantum Cryptography over the air, Cisco provides Qualcomm Technologies-powered access points while the complete client-side solution is supported by an Intel Wi-Fi chipset and driver and Microsoft for Windows software.

Expanded support for Live Protect: Live Protect reduces the gap between vulnerability disclosure and patch completion on supported Cisco platforms and releases. Live Protect is now supported on N9000 Series Switches, N9300 Smart Switches, Catalyst SD-WAN, C9000 Series Smart Switches, and CW9800 Wireless Controllers. Support on Cisco 8000 Secure Routers and Cisco Firewalls is intended to be available by the end of 2026.

Privileged infrastructure access: Being developed in collaboration with Teleport, Cisco Privileged Infrastructure Access gives network teams and AI agents fast, governed, task-specific access to Cisco routers and switches, with short-lived, identity-bound certificates. Sessions are recorded, and privilege expires when the session ends.

Supporting Quotes

“Ecosystem Deal Registration is an important step forward in recognizing the value partners like Deloitte create throughout the customer lifecycle, from shaping opportunities and defining solutions to helping customers realize value. By making these contributions more visible, Cisco is creating stronger foundations for collaboration and shared growth.” -- Filipe Gomes Leonardo,Associate Partner - Cyber and Telecom Networks, Deloitte

“We are excited about Cisco's continued innovation and look forward to Cisco Partner Summit. With expanded partner access to Cisco IQ, we can build lifecycle integrations and professional services that turn reactive analysis into proactive insight. Together, we help clients manage risk, plan upgrades and get more value from every dollar they spend,” said Kevin Corace, Senior Vice President, Software and Services Lifecycle, Presidio.

“As our enterprise customers scale AI workloads and high-density wireless environments, the network must evolve from simple connectivity into an active, self-defending platform. Cisco’s innovations embed industry-leading security and continuous visibility directly into the physical infrastructure our customers need. Combined with NTT DATA’s Agentic Operations, this creates an intelligent operating environment that can sense, predict and act, proactively addressing experience degradation and securing mission-critical operations before disruption occurs.” – Dilip Kumar, President and Global Head Infrastructure Solutions, NTT DATA, Inc.

Amy Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, shared the below communication with Microsoft employees today.

Today, we’re introducing a new Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to eligible employees within participating organizations. This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs.

The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.

What employees should know

This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below. This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources. Some organizations are providing the Voluntary Exit Offer, and some are not. Participation varies based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.

Eligible employees will receive an email with a link to their Voluntary Exit Offer details within the next few hours.

Looking ahead

The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft. There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee. These are a few of the ways we’re trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute.

My promise is to continue to provide clarity, listen and learn and keep improving.

Thank you for everything you continue to do for our customers, Microsoft and for one another.

Amy

articles.context: ref Signature reference IDs, up to 10 The first full transaction detections focus on exploit confirmation for high profile vulnerability
articles.full_text:
Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules. Full transaction detections evaluate each HTTP request alongside its response to identify evidence of exploitation. It helps answer both "Does this request look malicious?" and "What happened when the application handled it?" Response rules can then block the origin’s response before it reaches the requester.

These are valuable protections because the latest frontier models are uncovering vulnerabilities buried deep in widely used software, giving defenders clarity on what to fix — and attackers new paths to exploit. The recent php2shell vulnerability shows the stakes: a flaw in a common software component can put applications across the Internet at risk. AI agents scanning for vulnerabilities can be extremely persistent, adapting payloads using feedback, and chaining vulnerabilities, credentials, and permissions. An application's response can reveal whether an attempt worked and give an attacker information that helps them go deeper.

Inspecting incoming requests remains essential for stopping recognizable attacks before they reach an application. But some threats become clear only when the request is considered alongside what the origin returns. A suspicious input followed by a response exposing sensitive information tells a different story from the same input followed by a rejection or an error.

With these new capabilities, customers can use Cloudflare-managed protections or build their own policies combining request and response properties. This extends our always-on application security framework, with detection results available in Security Analytics to support investigation. Our first managed protections using this capability address the recently disclosed php2shell vulnerability.

And the best part? We are making these new capabilities generally available to all Cloudflare customers, including Free plans.

Request inspection is not enough

Cloudflare WAF protects websites and APIs with managed rules, custom rules, and rate limiting. Managed rules provide protection for known attack techniques and vulnerabilities while custom rules let teams create their own policies using parameters such as an IP address, URL path, headers, and request body. These controls operate at the request level to stop exploits or unwanted traffic from reaching the origin.

For many threats, this is the right place to act. However, treating every suspicious request as a confirmed exploit creates a difficult choice. Broad request signatures can catch more potential attacks, but they can also show “false positives”, such as matching legitimate traffic — which then breaks the applications. Deploying only rules that do not trigger false positives reduces that risk, but can leave more room for more ambiguous traffic to reach the server.

The response provides the missing evidence. Cloudflare can now correlate it with the request that produced it, so detections can account for the outcome of the entire HTTP transaction.

As an illustrative example, consider an application that lets users download files. An attacker manipulates the file parameter to request a private configuration file outside the permitted directory:

GET /download?file=../../config/database.ini

Request inspection can recognize this path traversal attempt and block it before it reaches the application. The request alone, however, cannot establish whether the application would expose the file. It might reject the request, ignore the traversal, or return an error. If the request reaches the origin, a response like this provides additional evidence:

200 OK Content-Type: text/plain [database] username=app_service password=EXAMPLE_SECRET

Full transaction detection provides a missing piece: it can correlate the attempted file access with response content characteristic of a private configuration file. Configuration-like text can legitimately appear in documentation or example downloads; combining it with a traversal attempt provides stronger evidence of sensitive data exposure than either signal alone. A response rule can then replace the origin response with a Cloudflare WAF block page and HTTP 403 before it reaches the requester, effectively blocking the exploit by preventing sensitive information from reaching the attacker.

Detection and mitigation are separate by design

Full transaction detection extends the always-on detection framework we introduced earlier this year. Detections analyze traffic and attach metadata to the request and response, rules then decide what to do with those results.

Separating those jobs gives customers visibility before they design a policy. Security teams can inspect detections in their own traffic, understand which endpoints and signatures are involved, and choose the response that fits their application. Similar to the approach for the request-based Attack Signature Detection, the outcome of the detections are stored in fields that can be accessed in the response custom rules or used in managed detections to block traffic.

Mirroring the request detection fields, the following new fields are added to our platform:

Field

Description

cf.waf.signature.response.confidence

Confidence values associated with matching signatures

cf.waf.signature.response.categories

Categories associated with matching signatures

cf.waf.signature.response.ref

Signature reference IDs, up to 10

The first full transaction detections focus on exploit confirmation for high profile vulnerability. It correlates suspicious input with response signals that indicate an exploit may have succeeded.

We will expand coverage over time by supporting other use cases, including detecting data exposure and exfiltration signals. This is important for the Internet beyond any one application: defenses can distinguish probing from evidence of impact, while detection of exposed data and services can reach customers that do not have a dedicated security team tuning every WAF rule.

Create rules on the response

Detecting evidence of exploitation is most useful if you can act on it in real time. Response custom rules turn full transaction detections into inline protection by blocking a matching origin response before it reaches the requester, although it cannot undo actions already performed at the origin.

Security teams can now combine request and response properties with detection results to decide which responses to block. When a blocking rule matches, Cloudflare replaces the origin response with a WAF block page or a custom response.

Response phase controls are available in the Cloudflare dashboard at the bottom of the Security > Security Rules page, with both managed protections and custom rules.

We have released both managed and custom rules to all plans, including Free plans. Over time, we will follow the same approach we use for request detections, where managed detections for free plans focus on high-profile vulnerabilities, while paying customers get a richer catalog of detections.

Managed detections

All customers get the protection of the full array of transaction detections through the Cloudflare Managed Response Firewall Default ruleset, which is designed for a simple one-click deploy and simplified configurability. When a signature matches, the managed detection will block the response and return a standard WAF block page.

You can edit the Cloudflare Managed Response Firewall Default scope to run detections only on a portion of their applications, for example by excluding or restricting the detection to a specific path. Paying customers can use detection fields in custom response rules to create more tailored policies.

Custom rules

Custom response rules are designed to give customers full control of the rule logic. A useful rule can stop an administration interface from being exposed when an authentication gateway has not marked the request as internal. For example:

http.request.uri.path starts_with "/admin" and not http.request.headers["x-internal-user"][0] eq "true" and http.response.code eq 200 and http.response.headers["content-type"][0] contains "text/html"

This blocks only when an unauthenticated request targets `/admin` and the origin actually returns a successful HTML administration page. It does not block ordinary authentication failures, redirects, or non-administration traffic.

All customers can create up to three custom response rules supporting Log and Block actions. The fields and functions available in response to custom rules mirrors what your plan gives you access to in request custom rules already. Creating rules on the response body is not yet available.

Following the Attack Signature Detection approach, paying customers also have access to the outcome of attack detections through the cf.waf.signature.response.* fields listed above. These fields can be combined with other parameters (such as a hostname, URL path, source IP, request header) to enable protection on a single path, or limit the policy to application-specific context. We are currently rolling out the response fields to all our accounts. If you don’t have access to them yet, please contact your account team.

Investigating matching requests

When a managed or custom response rule logs or blocks a transaction, the event is available in Security Events. This means responders can trace any detection back to the full context of the request and the specific rule that took action.

At the moment, both request-only rules and full-transaction rules are shown together in the same analytics page. In Security Events, the events generated by response rules are part of the Managed Rules or Custom Rules service. You can filter events belonging to a specific rule ID in the relative rule list section.

Get started today

Full transaction detection is generally available for all zones proxying traffic through Cloudflare. To verify that you’re protected, go to Security > Security Rules in the Cloudflare dashboard. If you want to customize your policy, start by reviewing full transaction detections in Security Analytics, then create the response phase policy that fits your application.

articles.context: ZIP files shared between co-workers containing new agent skills, locally-developed MCP servers passed between developers, and locally stored newly-minted agents are all...
articles.full_text:
ZIP files shared between co-workers containing new agent skills, locally-developed MCP servers passed between developers, and locally stored newly-minted agents are all seemingly harmless files that are commonly used in corporate software development environments.

Unfortunately, far from being harmless, these locally stored files can contain AI assets that were never detected or registered as an approved artifact in your applications.

Such skills are what we refer to as “Shadow AI,” and often they reside on private developer workstations, which are often not governed by central controls. The good news is that you can now detect “local Shadow AI”. By deploying JFrog AI Security, you can extend Shadow AI detection from your repositories to the laptops and workstations where these coding agents actually run, and the work gets done. Let’s break it down.

Ungated Executables: How AI Assets Bypass Security Controls

Until recently, building software followed a strict, secure process: approved code and tools come from trusted official sources, get scanned for vulnerabilities, and must pass company security policies before anyone is allowed to use them.

In today’s “AI-Era”, you can no longer rely on this traditional process for AI assets. Because AI tools and developers can instantly introduce unvetted files, scripts, and plugins on-demand – often straight from GitHub, Slack threads, or even generated by the agent itself – these assets completely bypass standard security checks. This turns a controlled, predictable workflow into something instant, random, and unmonitored.

Some examples include:

Skills: bundles of instructions and scripts that define how an agent performs a task.

MCP servers: Model Context Protocol servers, the connectors that enable agents to interact with systems such as databases, Jira, or Slack.

Plugins: installable packages that bundle skills, MCP servers, and more.

All of these unchecked assets represent serious potential security issues. Perhaps this is best exemplified by Hooks, where authors single-handedly decide what runs on which machine every time the agent is invoked – without ever consulting the rest of the team.

In essence, we wind up with two paths: the Managed Path where assets are scanned and vetted, and the Local Path where Shadow AI components go undetected.

Two paths for AI assets: one governed by JFrog, one with no gates and no reviews

Security Beyond the Repo: Protecting Developer Workstations

Previously, JFrog AI Security detected Shadow AI in your software supply chain by scanning AI models in your JFrog Artifactory repositories and calls to external AI services in your builds. That established a baseline for what we detect in the managed path of your software supply chain, and it worked pretty well, until now.

Shadow AI is more challenging to detect than third-party code and open-source packages, which are introduced into the development environment through a well established centralized build process and not stored on local machines.

Previously, the main risks on developer machines were due to extensions or tools over which DevOps had full control. The risk today is that malicious or non-compliant AI assets, used by coding agents, represent a new type of risk happening autonomously without visibility or control over developer laptops and workstations. This requires an added layer of protection that transparently detects Shadow AI on local machines without affecting developer productivity.

In addition to detecting AI assets on developer machines, JFrog AI Security also provides essential information to security teams and platform administrators regarding potential threats, including:

What risk does it carry? A skill that can run shell commands carries much greater risk than one that can only read files.

Is it allowed by organizational policy? A GitHub MCP server on a laptop may be acceptable if it matches the one you approved, but is a problem if someone built it from a random repository. JFrog plans to add this capability in a future release.

Here is how it works in practice:

Detection is enabled by installing the JFrog Agent Plugin on each developer workstation and operates by following these three steps:

Discover. Detects potentially risky skills, MCP servers, plugins, hooks, commands, and monitors.

Scan Locally. Runs a light deterministic rules-based scan on each workstation where the plugin is installed, designed so that the same input gets the same result every time.

Report. Sends metadata, asset identity, findings, and risk analysis to the JFrog Platform.

How Shadow AI assets on developer workstations become visible

Centralized Visibility Across Managed & Unmanaged AI Assets

JFrog AI Security turns detailed AI asset reports into a single unified inventory. Each record shows the asset’s name, type, harness that reported it (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), number of workstations where it was detected, local risk analysis, JFrog origin, and detection timestamp.

Two key metrics help prioritize the potential threats to address:

Risk Assessment reveals the underlying security findings for each rating upon selection:

Shell Access + WebFetch: High risk of data exfiltration.

Unscoped Write/Edit: Modifies files outside designated directories.

BypassPermissions Mode: Executes actions without required approval.

Origin documents if the asset already exists in the JFrog Platform:

JFrog Artifactory or JFrog Catalog: The selected asset matches an asset already managed by the JFrog Platform.

No Match: The asset does not match any asset managed in your JFrog Platform.

Gain Complete Visibility Over Your AI Assets

Your developers might already be using AI assets that have not been vetted or approved. Detecting Shadow AI on workstations can help you understand the severity and risk associated with each unmanaged AI asset.

JFrog AI Security ensures managed and unmanaged AI assets follow the same rules as every other artifact you ship: one unified supply chain, one system of record with no Shadow AI exceptions.

articles.title: Introducing ITDR Lookback: Find Out Who Was in Your Microsoft 365 Tenant Before You Were
articles.context: Today, Huntress Managed ITDR's Lookback feature is generally available for newly onboarded Microsoft 365 tenants
articles.full_text:
Today, Huntress Managed ITDR's Lookback feature is generally available for newly onboarded Microsoft 365 tenants. Lookback automatically examines up to 180 days of login history to uncover evidence of compromise before Huntress connected. When a compromise is still active, our Security Operations Center (SOC) investigates and revokes the identity's active sessions.

Onboarding a Microsoft 365 tenant feels like a fresh start. You go through your checklist, and a successful connection tells you monitoring has started. But it doesn't tell you if an attacker got there first. Your first day protecting a tenant might be an attacker's twenty-seventh day inside.

That's what Lookback seeks to solve. You get a clearer picture of the tenant you've inherited, plus defenders who act on what they find. And yes, that includes trial tenants.

Six months of login history. A much stronger start.

Lookback runs once, automatically, when a Microsoft 365 tenant finishes onboarding to Managed ITDR. There's nothing extra to configure and no separate scan to remember to launch.

Huntress Managed ITDR's new Lookback feature is generally available, bringing up to 180 days of Microsoft 365 login history into the hunt for existing compromises.

Lookback applies Huntress's full set of Unwanted Access detections to the tenant's available Microsoft 365 login history, looking back up to 180 days. That includes detections for credential theft, token theft, adversary-in-the-middle attacks, suspicious browsers, and datacenter logins.

Here's the tricky part: evidence of an old compromise doesn't necessarily mean an attacker still has access. Someone may have already reset the password or revoked the compromised sessions. Treating every historical finding as a fresh emergency would make onboarding pretty miserable.

Lookback separates findings based on whether the compromise is still active:

Active compromises receive a critical Incident Report investigated by the Huntress AI-centric SOC, with the identity's active sessions revoked. This turns historical evidence into a reason to act right away.

Previously remediated compromises appear in the Identity Security Assessment as historical context. They don't trigger a new incident or an unnecessary lockdown for something you've already fixed.

That distinction matters. A raw list of suspicious logins leaves the sorting to you. Lookback does it first, so you can see what happened and which parts still need attention.

What's in the report, and where do you find it?

Lookback adds a dedicated section to the Identity Security Assessment, covering compromises that predate Huntress monitoring. It shows the period reviewed and previously remediated incidents, including affected identities, relevant dates, and observed remediation evidence, such as a password reset or session revocation. The report gives you a documented history you can use in a customer conversation or share with leadership.

That history sits alongside the assessment's existing coverage of identities, Rogue Apps, Shadow Workflows such as malicious inbox rules, Unwanted Access, and SOC findings and containment actions. Active compromises uncovered by Lookback also receive their own Incident Reports.

Lookback is part of onboarding for newly connected Microsoft 365 tenants. The assessment is generated automatically after onboarding and waits for Lookback to finish, so you receive one complete document. Once that historical review is complete, Managed ITDR continues monitoring for new threats with the Huntress SOC behind it.

The attackers who arrived before we did

In Lookback's first two weeks of early testing, Huntress reviewed more than 400 tenants. Among them were three very different organizations with the same unwelcome surprise: an active compromise already in progress.

A title company and a $2 million wire

A device-code phishing attack gave an adversary access three days before the tenant onboarded. The attacker persisted through a rogue Entra device and was watching a $2 million real estate wire transfer. Lookback surfaced the active compromise, which Huntress contained.

For a business moving that kind of money, "let's wait until the attacker does something else" is a lousy security strategy.

A school district with an unwanted administrator

A school district's Global Admin account had been compromised 27 days before onboarding. An unrevoked refresh token and a rogue Azure AD device kept the attacker's access alive, with the privileges to control the tenant. Lookback uncovered the compromise, and Huntress contained it. Twenty-seven days is a long head start. Connecting a new security tool shouldn't give the attacker more time simply because the break-in happened earlier.

An architecture firm turned into a phishing launchpad

An architecture firm onboarded with a nine-day foothold still active. The attack involved a hidden inbox rule and 103 external OneDrive phishing invitations sent in a single scripted second. The compromised account had become infrastructure for targeting other people. Lookback surfaced the compromise, which Huntress contained.

In all three cases, the attack began before onboarding. Looking backward gave our defenders evidence to act on right away, without waiting for an attacker's next move.

Less guesswork for you, more proof for your customers

If you're an MSP, every new client brings a history you didn't write. You still have to explain what you've inherited and what you plan to do about it.

Lookback helps you start that relationship with evidence from the client's own environment. You can show past compromises, distinguish resolved activity from active threats, and explain where Huntress has intervened. The shareable assessment makes that conversation easier, while SOC investigation and containment keep the historical review from becoming another helpdesk project.

Internal IT teams get the same benefit. Whether you've inherited a tenant through an acquisition, a vendor change, or staff turnover, you don't have to become a Microsoft audit log specialist to spot signs of prior compromise.

And if you're evaluating Huntress, your trial includes the same Lookback protection as a paid tenant. You can see what we find in your environment and how we respond to active threats while you're still making your decision.

Looking back is how we keep moving forward

Lookback is the latest step in our work to build best-in-class Managed ITDR that earns its place in your security stack every day.

The new ITDR dashboard puts identity activity and investigation tools closer at hand, including Rapid Identity Triage, Failed Login Characterization, and Quick SIEM Search. And the recently released ITDR Executive Summary makes technical incident findings easier to explain to business leaders, with plain-English context about what happened and the response.

Lookback extends that progress into the history you inherit at onboarding. Together, these releases help you understand existing threats, investigate current activity, and explain the work being done to protect the business.

Our standard for innovation is practical: does it help find an attacker, take work off your team, or give you an answer you couldn't easily get before? Lookback delivers on all three, backed by the same 24/7 SOC that protects your identities going forward.

Your tenant has a past, and now you can find out who's still living in it.

Ready to see what came before day one? Start a free trial of Huntress Managed ITDR and connect a Microsoft 365 tenant. Lookback runs automatically, with findings in your Identity Security Assessment and SOC response for active compromises.

articles.title: Trend Micro Announces Up to ¥10 Billion toward Cyber Resilience Initiative to Strengthen Security for Japanese Organizations in the AI Era
articles.context: The growing threat extends beyond large enterprises and critical infrastructure to smaller businesses, suppliers and service providers that form the foundation of Japan's economy
articles.full_text:
Initiative supports nationwide modernization of security measures for individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises, with additional access to TrendAI Vision One™ AI security capabilities and expert technical support provided through partners.

TOKYO, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trend Micro Incorporated (TSE: 4704) today announced plans for the Japan Cyber Resilience Initiative, a major national effort to help Japanese organizations strengthen their cybersecurity, reduce critical exposures and modernize their defenses for the AI era. This initiative is designed to support not only organizations but also individuals.

Japan's cybersecurity challenge is escalating rapidly. According to threat research from TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro, 607 publicly disclosed cybersecurity incidents were recorded during the first nine months of 2026, already exceeding the 594 reported throughout all of 2025*. Furthermore, the growing number of personal data breaches at organizations has exposed sensitive information on a large scale, creating cyber risks not only for enterprises but also for individuals and Japanese society as a whole.

*Cybersecurity incident figures are tallies as of October 9, 2026. Figures may change due to factors such as incidents that are later disclosed retroactively and additional cases being added.

Yet as attacks grow in volume and sophistication, many organizations remain unprepared for the next generation of threats. The growing threat extends beyond large enterprises and critical infrastructure to smaller businesses, suppliers and service providers that form the foundation of Japan's economy.

The program is designed to serve organizations and individuals across Japan, with an initial emphasis on critical infrastructure, major enterprises and the smaller businesses essential to their supply chains. Support will be provided in phases, tailored to organizational needs, eligibility and available resources.

Trend Micro will work closely with its extensive network of channel partners, systems integrators and managed service providers across Japan to extend the initiative's reach. Eligible organizations will receive up to 10 days of professional services free of charge*, delivered through partners to help them access the right cybersecurity expertise and support.

*For details, including requirements for use, please contact us.

Through its enterprise cybersecurity business, TrendAI™, the company proposes to make available up to ¥10 billion in TrendAI Flex licensing credits to help eligible organizations modernize their security environments with TrendAI Vision One™. The initiative also includes plans to mobilize forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) and provide access to managed detection and response (MDR) expertise.

A national challenge demands a national commitment

Japan's senior political leaders have characterized the situation as a cybersecurity emergency.

As a global cybersecurity company headquartered in Japan, Trend Micro has spent decades protecting Japanese businesses while investing extensively in global threat research, vulnerability discovery, threat intelligence and incident response.

"Japan is our home. When the organizations and individuals that power our economy, our infrastructure and our communities face an escalating cybersecurity challenge, we have a responsibility to step forward. No organization should have to face this challenge alone. We are bringing together our technology, our people and our global security expertise to help Japan strengthen its defenses today and prepare for a future in which cyber threats will move faster than ever." said Eva Chen, Trend Micro CEO.

The Japan Cyber Resilience Initiative will provide the following six forms of support to organizations and individuals.

＜For organizations＞

1. Up to ¥10 billion to accelerate cybersecurity modernization

Trend Micro proposes an aggregate allocation of up to ¥10 billion in TrendAI Flex licensing credits to help eligible organizations adopt and expand protection through the TrendAI Vision One™ platform designed to help customers modernize their existing security environments, strengthen protection across critical systems. Through TrendAI Flex Unlimited, customers will also be able to access additional TrendAI Vision One™ capabilities, including AI security innovations.

The initiative will also help existing customers, working with their trusted channel partners where appropriate, build on their current security investments and transition toward modern, AI-era defenses without unnecessarily disrupting established protection.

The proposed allocation represents licensing credits, not a cash grant. The initiative will be introduced in phases, with detailed eligibility criteria, credit allocation and redemption terms, partner participation options, and service availability to be communicated as the program is rolled out.

2. Forward-deployed engineers to turn technology into stronger defenses

Recognizing that cybersecurity modernization requires more than technology alone, TrendAI™ plans to mobilize forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) and technical specialists to work directly with participating organizations.

These specialists will work alongside participating organizations and their existing partners, where appropriate, to assess critical exposures, identify security gaps, prioritize risk reduction and accelerate the deployment of modern security capabilities.

FDE engagements will initially prioritize organizations whose security is particularly important to national infrastructure, economic activity and interconnected supply chains. For smaller organizations, Trend Micro intends to work through appropriate delivery models and its partner ecosystem to help extend the initiative's reach.

3. Expert-led detection, response and operational resilience

Through TrendAI™'s MDR capabilities and security expertise, eligible organizations will be able to explore additional support for continuous threat monitoring, incident investigation and response.

The initiative aims to help organizations move beyond isolated security controls toward a coordinated approach that connects exposure management, threat detection, incident response and proactive risk reduction.

Trend Micro also protects more than 10 million consumers across Japan through its TrendLife™ business unit. Through local partners and a network of managed service provider (MSP) partners serving over 230,000 small and medium-sized businesses, we also help protect close to 2 million business devices. Building on this foundation, we will continue to help strengthen security for consumers and small businesses alike.

4. 60-day free trial of Worry-Free Business Security Services provided (TBD)

Small and medium-sized businesses play a vital role in supply chains, and strengthening their security is increasingly urgent. For these customers, a 60-day free trial of Worry-Free Business Security Services will be provided. In addition, TrendLife™ is considering new support for the Worry-Free series together with its channel partners. Further details will be announced as they are finalized. Note: The free trial is available only to new customers in Japan and must be started by December 31, 2026.

5. Exploring AI-Powered Scam Protection to Strengthen Digital Trust on LINE

As small businesses increasingly rely on LINE Official Accounts (LINE OA) to engage with customers, everyday interactions may also expose them to scams disguised as customer inquiries, suspicious links, or fraudulent requests.

TrendLife™ is advancing API integrations with providers of LINE-related services, enabling AI-powered scam detection capabilities to be seamlessly embedded into customer touchpoints and helping strengthen protection for both businesses and their customers. We are currently working with partners, including Crescendo Lab, one of Asia's leading LINE CRM providers, and are in the final stages of preparation for commercial deployment by the end of the year.

＜For consumers＞

6. 90 days of Trend Micro ScamCheck provided free of charge

TrendLife™ will provide 90 days of complimentary access to Trend Micro ScamCheck, our mobile scam protection app. In the event that leaked personal information is misused in phone, email, or other scam attempts, Trend Micro ScamCheck helps protect users from potential scams.

The benefit will be provided through the following channels:

TrendLife Online Store: Customers who purchase through the site below will have their subscription extended by 90 days. https://shop.trendlife.com/ja-jp/products/scam-buster.asp

App stores: Please follow the instructions on the page below. https://trendlife.com/ja-jp/blog/news-tmsc-3-month-free-trial/

Note: In all cases, customers must start using the service by December 31, 2026. This offer is available only to customers in Japan.

A lasting commitment to Japan's cyber resilience

Trend Micro will work with customers and partners to translate this initiative into measurable improvements in cybersecurity, with plans to track participation, modernization progress and defensive outcomes.

Organizations and partners interested in participating can contact their Trend Micro representative or visit the Initiative Landing Page to register their interest and receive updates as program details and participation opportunities become available. For individual customers, please contact us through TrendLife™ website.

About Trend Micro

Trend Micro Incorporated is a Japan-headquartered global cybersecurity company dedicated to protecting the digital world. Drawing on decades of security expertise, worldwide threat intelligence and cybersecurity innovation, the company helps organizations and individuals protect their digital environments and build resilience against evolving cyber threats.

For more information, visit trendmicro.com or TrendLife™ (Japanese).

Over the past year, the Huntress API has grown from six read-only endpoints into a full integration and automation platform, along with Webhooks and an MCP server. For partners, that means Huntress data can show up wherever they already work, not just in our portal. It also means software vendors can build their own Huntress integrations on their own schedule, without having to wait on us.

Nine Minds is a great example. Their team built a Huntress integration for AlgaPSA, their professional services automation (PSA) platform, using our public API documentation. No technical support or special access needed. They just read the docs and, a few days later, had a working integration. This post covers what they built, what the experience was like, and what it shows about how you can use the Huntress API.

Meet Nine Minds and AlgaPSA

Nine Minds was founded by Robert Isaacs and Arnie Bellini, who both spent over a decade at ConnectWise. AlgaPSA is their answer to a problem they saw in the industry for years: PSA tools that are too expensive, too complicated, and primarily built for mature organizations.

AlgaPSA brings ticketing, projects, time tracking, billing, and client operations into one platform, and it was designed with the smallest MSPs in mind. As Robert told ChannelE2E, "The small MSP doesn't want to sign a three-year contract." But as they've progressed, larger MSPs have started taking notice, too.

AlgaPSA gives MSPs control over how they run the software with hosted, self-hosted, and open-source options. Over a hundred MSPs now rely on AlgaPSA for day-to-day operations, with more signing up every week.

Why Build a Huntress Integration?

For Nine Minds, the decision came down to two things. Mutual customers were asking for it, and their team spends a lot of time in the MSP community, including at IT Nation, and Huntress is one of the names they see everywhere.

When your users already rely on Huntress to catch threats, the next question is simple: how do those incidents get to the technicians who need to act on them? The AlgaPSA <> Huntress integration provides an answer.

How the Integration Works

The integration is built around the premise that a security incident should never go without a ticket. When the Huntress SOC publishes an incident report, it appears in AlgaPSA as a ticket on a dedicated security board, with the incident summary and a priority based on its severity.

Technicians work it like any other ticket, and the time they log flows into AlgaPSA's billing and invoicing. That means security responses get tracked and billed like the rest of their work, instead of living in a separate console. When the SOC closes the incident, the ticket can close automatically, too. And if an incident comes from a client that hasn't been mapped yet, it still lands on a triage board, so nothing slips through.

Setup takes a few steps:

Connect your Huntress API credentials

Map Huntress organizations to AlgaPSA clients

Choose where tickets land and how severities translate to priorities.

Nine Minds walks through each step in the AlgaPSA Huntress integration docs.

A few things to know before you start:

Use a dedicated API key. Huntress API keys are tied to a user and mirror that user's permissions, so it's a good idea to create a separate key just for this integration.

You need AlgaPSA's paid tier. The Huntress integration is part of AlgaPSA's Enterprise Edition (also offered as AlgaPSA Pro). It isn't included in the open-source Community Edition.

Finish routing first. AlgaPSA won't start pulling incidents until the security board, the fallback client and board, and priorities for all three Huntress severities (Critical, High, and Low) are set.

Expect tickets on a schedule, not instantly. AlgaPSA checks Huntress for new incident reports at an interval you choose between one and 60 minutes, so tickets show up at the next check.

What Was It Like to Build on the Huntress API?

This is the part we're most excited about. Nine Minds went from idea to a shipped integration in just a few days.

They built it using our public documentation, without reaching out to us first. After a short period working out which data they needed, Robert said things went smoothly: no confusing fields, no missing endpoints, no documentation gaps that slowed them down. Their team also uses AI coding tools, and pointing those tools at the Huntress API docs was enough to get the job done.

"Integrating Huntress into AlgaPSA was easy enough that we almost felt as if we had missed something... [Then] our customers started thanking us for the integration. Working with Huntress could not have been easier."

– Robert IsaacsFounder / CEO, Nine Minds

Nine Minds also built a Huntress emulator so they could test the integration without depending on live incidents. They told us a dedicated sandbox environment would make that easier, and we've shared that feedback with our team.

What Else Can You Build?

AlgaPSA's integration shows one common pattern: pull incidents from Huntress and turn them into tickets. But the API supports a lot more.

A few examples:

Get incidents in real time. Instead of polling, Huntress Webhooks push incidents and escalations to your PSA, Slack, or SIEM as they happen.

Act on incidents. Approve or reject remediations through the Incident Report response API, and isolate or release hosts through the Agents API.

Automate onboarding. Create, update, and delete organizations programmatically. For example, when a new client is added in your RMM, automation can create the matching Huntress organization and start EDR deployment.

Reconcile billing and build reports. Pull billing reports and per-product organization stats, like agent counts, SIEM storage, and ITDR identity counts, into your dashboards, QBRs, or PSA contracts.

Bring Huntress into AI workflows. The Huntress MCP server connects your AI assistant to your incidents, agents, billing data, and more.

Prefer to see how this works? Watch our video below to see inside the Huntress API, Webooks, and MCP server:

Ready to Learn More?

AlgaPSA's integration started with a customer request and ended with a shipped feature just a few days later. That's the kind of experience we want every developer to have with the Huntress API. If you've been thinking about connecting Huntress to your own tools, the docs are a good place to start.

Use Huntress with AlgaPSA: See the AlgaPSA Huntress integration docs for setup steps.

Share feedback: Have an idea for an endpoint, webhook, or integration? Add it to our Integrations, Webhooks, and APIs feedback board.

articles.title: Introducing Evo Agentic AppSec: Security That Keeps Up With AI Development
articles.context: Attackers are using AI to identify weaknesses, combine lower-severity issues into more serious exploits, and accelerate attacks
articles.full_text:
AI is changing how software gets built. Coding agents produce more code than teams can review, and current models introduce several times more vulnerabilities per line than human developers. Many of those flaws involve business logic, access control, and authentication, areas where pattern-based scanners have limited visibility.

Most security teams were already behind before any of this started. They are flooded with findings, many of which are noise, while managing a backlog of latent risk. Attackers are using AI to identify weaknesses, combine lower-severity issues into more serious exploits, and accelerate attacks. As of October 2026, Snyk’s data showed roughly eight new vulnerabilities introduced for every one remediated. AI-driven development adds further pressure to that imbalance. And the in-depth security reviews that catch business logic flaws take so much time and context that most teams run them once, for a handful of critical apps.

Software supply chain attacks compound the problem. Malicious packages now account for most open source zero-days, with more than 20 high-profile attacks in 2026 and growth on track to exceed 600% year over year. A malicious package can steal credentials during installation, before a pull request or CI scan runs, and coding agents can introduce these packages without assessing whether they are safe.

Security needs to keep pace with how software is now built and address risks before code reaches review.

The pull request scan is no longer enough on its own

Pull request scanning remains an important control. On its own, however, it cannot address every risk, particularly when code is generated continuously, and malicious dependencies can cause harm before a scan begins.

Application security has to run in three places: checks inside the coding workflow, fast deterministic scans on every change in CI, and deeper analysis of the full application at regular intervals. That analysis must also account for business logic and application context alongside known vulnerability patterns.

Finding more issues is only useful if teams can act on them. Prevention and remediation need to scale too, with clear policies governing what gets blocked, what gets fixed, and what requires human review. Proposed fixes need independent validation before teams accept them.

The answer is not another scanner. It’s the program, run by agents and owned by your team.

Introducing Evo Agentic AppSec

Evo Agentic AppSec is a team of security agents that does the work of your application security program, so your team can focus on setting policy and owning the decisions. It brings these capabilities together to help teams manage application security continuously, from threat assessment and prevention through detection, prioritization, remediation, and verification.

It helps teams assess an application’s threats and controls, identify vulnerabilities, prioritize fixes, and validate the results. The agents work across new code during development, helping to prevent new issues and block the install of malicious packages, and across the applications you have already shipped, so the backlog actually goes down.

Snyk’s security intelligence provides the context behind this work. It combines ten years of deterministic assessments with signals such as reachability, exploitability, breakability, and fix outcomes. That context helps teams separate the issues that matter from the noise, and turns a proposed change into a fix a team can use.

In VulnBump, Snyk’s newest benchmark of real dependency upgrades, Evo Remediation Agent produced mergeable fixes 90% of the time, compared with 59.6% for the same model without Snyk context. A mergeable fix resolves the vulnerability and leaves the project able to build.

Independent verification is central to this approach. Deterministic engines check proposed fixes rather than relying solely on the model that generated them. Teams define the policies and acceptance criteria that govern the process.

Agentic AppSec is the next solution coming to Evo, the part of the Snyk platform built to help teams secure both the applications they develop and the AI agents they deploy.

How it works

Evo Agentic AppSec brings together a team of agents with specific roles:

Evo Agentic Security Review assesses an application’s threats and controls, producing evidence-backed findings and remediation guidance. Now, that depth of review can run across every application, without scaling your team.

Evo Code Scanning Agent identifies business logic and authorization flaws that traditional scanners miss.

Snyk Secrets detects exposed secrets across traditional and AI-assisted development.

Evo Remediation Agent fixes issues in new code and the existing backlog, starting with third-party dependency issues at launch.

Evo Dependency Firewall blocks malicious and out-of-policy packages at install time, before code scanning ever comes into play. You don’t have to tell your agents to be careful about what they install; they pull from trusted packages by default.

Evo Continuous Offensive Security provides adversarial testing to further assess the application’s defenses and the effectiveness of remediation.

Together, these capabilities help teams expand security coverage and handle more remediation work, while keeping a human on the loop, retaining control over policies, priorities, and approvals.

Evo Agentic AppSec builds on Snyk Code and Snyk Open Source. The engines that teams already use to scan code and dependencies provide the underlying analysis and independently validate findings and proposed fixes.

Giving teams more capacity

As more development and security work becomes automated, teams need clear oversight and accountability.

Developers can spend more time reviewing proposed changes. AppSec teams can focus on security policy, exceptions, and the risks that require their judgment. CISOs gain visibility into a continuously running program, with adversarial testing and an audit trail of automated decisions.

For organizations without a dedicated AppSec function, these capabilities can help establish consistent security practices and reduce the manual work needed to maintain them.

The goal is practical: prevent more issues, resolve existing vulnerabilities faster, and give teams evidence that their fixes work.

Your backlog is growing faster than it can be burned down

Evo Agentic AppSec brings prevention, detection, remediation, and verification to help teams address those challenges.
